questions.stem: Internal energy is the sum of:

options.text: The mass and volume of the substance
The total kinetic energy and total potential energy of all particles
The gravitational potential energy and elastic energy
The temperature and pressure of the substance

questions.explanation: Internal energy equals the total kinetic energy of all particles (due to their motion) plus the total potential energy (due to bonds and forces between particles).

options.text: The average kinetic energy of the particles
The total internal energy of a substance
The potential energy between particles
The total number of particles

questions.explanation: Temperature is a measure of the average kinetic energy of the particles in a substance. Higher temperature means faster particles on average.

questions.stem: When a substance is heated and its temperature rises, which component of internal energy increases?

options.text: Both kinetic and potential energy equally
Only the kinetic energy of particles
Neither -- the energy is destroyed
Only the potential energy of particles

questions.explanation: When temperature rises, particles move faster, so their kinetic energy increases. The potential energy component changes mainly during changes of state.

questions.stem: During a change of state, the energy supplied increases the:

options.text: Kinetic energy of particles (temperature rises)
Number of particles
Mass of the substance
Potential energy of particles (bonds are broken)

questions.explanation: During a change of state, the temperature stays constant, so kinetic energy does not change. The energy goes into increasing the potential energy by breaking bonds between particles.

options.text: Dense objects to less dense objects
Cold objects to hot objects
Hot objects to cold objects
Large objects to small objects

questions.explanation: Heat (thermal energy) always flows naturally from a region of higher temperature to a region of lower temperature, until thermal equilibrium is reached.

questions.stem: Two objects are at the same temperature. Which statement is correct?

options.text: They are made of the same material
They have the same internal energy
Their particles have the same average kinetic energy
They have the same number of particles

questions.explanation: Objects at the same temperature have particles with the same average kinetic energy. They do not necessarily have the same total internal energy, as that also depends on the number of particles and potential energy.

questions.stem: Which state of matter has the greatest internal energy per particle (for the same substance)?

options.text: Liquid
All states have equal internal energy per particle
Solid
Gas

questions.explanation: Gases have the greatest internal energy per particle because particles have high kinetic energy (fast motion) and high potential energy (bonds fully broken).
